name: oracle_manipulation
description: Manipulable spot-price oracle (DEX reserves) used for value-critical calculations without TWAP or safeguards
question: The source file in `source` computes a token price directly from a DEX pool's instantaneous reserves or tick state (e.g., via getReserves(), slot0, or raw balance ratios) and feeds that spot price directly into a value-bearing calculation such as collateral valuation, liquidation threshold, minting, or borrow limit, without any time-weighted averaging (no TWAP/consult call), without cross-checking a secondary oracle, and without staleness or deviation checks, allowing an attacker to manipulate the price within a single transaction (e.g., via a flash loan) to under-collateralize positions, trigger unfair liquidations, or drain protocol funds.
criteria: Calls getReserves(), slot0(), or reads raw pool token balances to derive a price
The derived price is used directly (same transaction, no averaging) in collateral valuation, liquidation, minting, or borrowing logic
No call to a TWAP/consult function or time-weighted price library
No fallback or cross-check against a second independent oracle (e.g., Chainlink)
No staleness, deviation, or sanity-bound checks applied before using the price
Comment or logic indicates the price can change within one block/transaction and is trusted anyway
